findings.text: `repoRoot()` in Server/review.mjs:223 (`path.dirname(git(cwd, "rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-common-dir").stdout.trim())`) resolves to the MAIN tree, not the worktree, whenever it's run from inside a git worktree — `--git-common-dir` is shared by all worktrees of a repo. So `--score`/`--backfill`, run from the review-turns worktree (which is exactly where this task itself was built), silently read/write `C:/Code/lew42/monorepo/public/framework/ai/collab/scoreboard.jsonl` and scan the main tree's `ai/` for review.md — not the worktree's own copies. I reproduced this while checking the required proof: running `node Server/review.mjs --backfill` from the worktree wrote 4 real `{"score":{"kind":"review",...}}` lines straight into the main tree's live scoreboard.jsonl (untracked, so no diff showed it), which I had to delete afterward. This is exactly the setup the sub-mastermind uses (multi-file/shared-module work goes to a worktree), so it will happen for real, not just in testing.

The proof requirements.md asks for — "one real review run through all four turns, with a held decline the mastermind ruled on; the scoreboard view with today's reviews backfilled from their review.md files" — was never actually done. No `review.jsonl` exists anywhere in the repo or worktree, no `{"score":{"kind":"review",...}}` line exists in the real scoreboard.jsonl, and `--backfill` was never run against the seven real review.md files that already exist in the main tree (fresh-eyes-review, collab-rounds, organization, etc.) — I ran it myself just now and it worked (4 scored, 3 skipped for unanswered findings), so the code can do it, but nobody actually landed that proof. task.jsonl for this task has no log lines from minion A at all describing phase-3/phase-4/score runs, only minion B's work.

Requirement 1 ("The mastermind decides... One line in the sub-mastermind skill: decide at the split, and write the why") doesn't appear to be covered by this deliverable. `.claude/skills/sub-mastermind/SKILL.md:54` only says to decide size and run review.mjs; it says nothing about `--why` or writing the reason down. The `--why` CLI flag itself already existed before this diff (untouched by it), so this may have been intended to land earlier, but the fence for this task explicitly lists "one line in sub-mastermind" as owed here.

`decisionIdFor` (Server/review.mjs:228, `"review-" + slug(basename(taskDir))`) is keyed only by the task's directory name, with no run identifier. If a task is ever reviewed a second time for real (not just answering the same findings — e.g. size raised, or new scope after the first round settled), the second `--score` will collide with the first run's `collab`+`decision` pair and `alreadyScored` will skip it, silently losing the second review's usefulness data. Worth a one-line mention of this limit in the doc, or a run counter in the id, if a second full review round is ever expected to happen for the same task.

`review.jsonl`'s finding/answer/reply/ruling maps (`readTurns`) are flat across the whole file, keyed only by finding number `n` — they're not scoped to a particular phase-1 run. If `review.mjs` (not `--turns`) is ever run a second time on the same taskDir (a fresh review pass, not just re-mirroring answers), the new run's finding `n=1,2,3…` will overwrite the previous run's finding text for the same numbers in `readTurns().findings`, which phase 3's prompt reads from — a decline in the new round could get labeled with the wrong finding's text. Likely fine under the current one-round model the doc describes, but not defended against if it stops holding.

assign.title: Review turns: findings answered in turns, scored on the Collab board
assign.outcome:
**Landed on michael/dev.** `Server/review.mjs` now runs a review as four logged turns instead of one shot: the reviewer's findings, the builder's answer to each (fixed/declined/noted), a fresh reviewer's reply to every decline (accept/hold), and the mastermind's ruling on anything still held — all written to `<taskdir>/review.jsonl`. Every settled review scores itself onto the shared Collab board, and a Reviews section (live now on [/framework/ext/Collab/](http://monorepo.localhost/framework/ext/Collab/)) shows reviews/%-useful/$-per-useful-review per model.

- [x] 1. The mastermind decides the review size (`none` needs `--why`, raising needs nothing) — already in review.mjs; one line added to [sub-mastermind](/.claude/skills/sub-mastermind/SKILL.md).
- [x] 2. Feedback in turns (findings → answers → reviewer replies → mastermind rulings, stopping after one round of holds) — `Server/review.mjs --turns` / `--rule`; proof: [review.jsonl](/public/framework/ai/2026-09-28/review-turns/review.jsonl) and a dedicated fixture at [proof/](/public/framework/ai/2026-09-28/review-turns/proof/review.jsonl) with a real held decline the mastermind ruled `fix`.
- [x] 3a. A usefulness score per review on the shared scoreboard — `--score`/`--backfill`; [scoreboard.jsonl](/public/framework/ai/collab/scoreboard.jsonl) now carries 6 real `kind:"review"` rows (4 backfilled from real historical reviews, 2 from this task's own).
- [x] 3b. A small Reviews view on the Collab scoreboard page — live at [/framework/ext/Collab/](http://monorepo.localhost/framework/ext/Collab/), screenshot: ![](final-shot/monorepo-localhost-framework-ext-Collab/sheet.png).
- [x] 4. Docs: [Server/doc/review.md](/Server/doc/review.md) rewritten turns-first.
- [x] Proof: one real review through all four turns with a held decline ruled on (above) + the scoreboard view backfilled with today's real reviews (above).

**Left deliberately:** `changed_outcome` is a `fixed > 0` proxy, not a real check against whether a fix actually merged (declined finding 5, with why, in [review.jsonl](/public/framework/ai/2026-09-28/review-turns/review.jsonl)) — a merge-time hook is a next brief's job. Two real bugs this task's own review caught along the way (a screenshot caller shooting the wrong tree, `status()` miscounting `noted` answers) turned out to match an owner-reported pattern from the `organization` task and are both fixed.
